discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 071000
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
600 AM EDT Wed Oct 7 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry and pleasant weather continues through Saturday with 
  highs generally in the 70s and lows in the mid 40s to low 50s.

- The next chance of rain arrives on Sunday associated with the
  remnants of a tropical system. No significant impacts are
  expected with this event.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 113 AM EDT Wed Oct 7 2026

Quiet weather to persist through the end of the week. A 130+ kt 
upper level jet and attendant PV anomaly passes through the Great 
Lakes later today. However, we remain in the unfavorable right exit 
region of this jet streak. Better CVA also passes to the north and 
lags well behind the associated surface front. Modest return flow 
ahead of this front will push highs near 80F (particularly in our 
S/SW) but surface dewpoints remain in the 50s and forecast soundings 
show very dry/stable and capped profiles. No precip expected with 
this frontal passage and likely just some high-based clouds at times 
through tonight. Another broad low level anticyclone then settles 
into the Upper Midwest on Thursday on the downstream side of large 
western CONUS ridge. Highs on Thu drop back to around 70F with 
dewpoints around 40F. Surface high passes over our area Thu night 
and return flow starts again by late Friday. Several deterministic 
00Z models generate some light QPF along the associated warm front/ 
theta-e surge but NBM is holding dry. Wouldn't be surprised if we 
have to add a low chance PoP or sprinkle mention Fri night but will 
hold off for now.

Attention then turns to the remnants of what will likely become 
Hurricane Isaias in the Gulf over the next few days. Latest 00Z 
guidance showing a westward shift in the associated rain shield that 
now clips much of our area with at least some light rain on Sunday. 
NBM PoP's now over 60% for much of our SE CWA. Still not expecting 
any appreciable impacts from this event though. Even a widespread 1-
1.5" should be tolerable given recent dry conditions and that is 
definitely on the high-end of possible outcomes. QPF amounts could 
easily be much lower. Some breezy conditions also possible but again 
not strong enough to be impactful.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z THURSDAY/... 
Issued at 559 AM EDT Wed Oct 7 2026

VFR conditions are expected at the terminals, with strengthening
southerly flow shifting west into the afternoon and evening
hours. Gusts up to around 21kts possible in the afternoon,
mainly at KFWA.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...AGD
AVIATION...MCD

spc.text:
SPC AC 070445

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1145 PM CDT Tue Oct 06 2026

   Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not expected across the U.S. today.

   ...Synopsis...
   A mid-level trough will amplify over the Northeast while broad upper
   ridging overspreads much of the western and central CONUS today.
   This upper-air pattern will support surface troughing over the
   Northeast, and encourage surface high pressure to overspread the
   remainder of the U.S. With the upper trough over the northern Great
   Lakes/Northeast, and with a subtle impulse over the Four Corners to
   the central Plains, a few thunderstorms are possible given colder
   temperatures aloft with these aforementioned features. The best
   chance for thunderstorms will be along a moistened baroclinic zone
   ahead of a weak surface low over central FL. 

   ...Western FL Peninsula Coastline...
   Similar to yesterday, a weak surface low will remain in place over
   the eastern Gulf, amid a moist low-level airmass, characterized by
   70s F surface dewpoints and minimal MLCINH. With afternoon heating,
   thunderstorm development should occur. As in previous days, lapse
   rates will be poor, with buoyancy driven by the rich low-level
   moisture, contributing to thin (500-1000 J/kg) MLCAPE profiles.
   Vertical wind shear will also be modest, though low-level veering
   may yield some low-level hodograph curvature and associated
   transient supercell potential. While waterspout potential will exist
   offshore, it is unclear if tornadic waterspout-producing storms will
   reach the western FL Peninsula coast, so severe probabilities will
   be withheld for now. However, severe probabilities may need to be
   added in later outlooks when meso-beta scale details regarding
   onshore severe potential become clearer.

   ..Squitieri/Wendt.. 10/07/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 070428

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1128 PM CDT Tue Oct 06 2026

   Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not expected on Thursday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low will move east out of James Bay and into Quebec on
   Thursday, with a broad upper trough from the Great Lakes into the
   Northeast. A leading midlevel speed max is forecast to move across
   southern New England during the day, with cold temperatures aloft to
   the north. This may favor isolated low-topped thunderstorms from the
   Upper Hudson Valley into Maine as surface heating occurs and a wind
   shift/trough sweeps across the region. Very small hail cannot be
   ruled out with 500 mb temperatures near -25 C.

   To the south, strong low-level easterlies will develop over the
   northern Gulf of America as the tropical cyclone strengthens over
   the central Gulf, possibly into a hurricane by Thursday evening per
   NHC. This flow regime will maintain 70s F dewpoints over FL, with
   scattered afternoon thunderstorms possible. Severe storms are not
   expected due to weak shear and poor lapse rates.

   To the west, cool midlevel temperatures to -12 C will exist over the
   Great Basin, with sparse weak thunderstorms over parts of the Four
   Corners states during the afternoon.

   Elsewhere, a few thunderstorms may occur from eastern NE into IA
   late in the day and overnight as southwesterly 850 mb winds increase
   to 30 kt, with sufficient elevated instability present in the warm
   advection/height rise regime.

   ..Jewell.. 10/07/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 070734

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0234 AM CDT Wed Oct 07 2026

   Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ALONG THE
   NORTH-CENTRAL GULF COAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   An increasing tornado risk may develop into early Saturday morning
   along the north-central Gulf Coast in association with the
   developing tropical cyclone.

   ...Discussion...
   Severe storm chances will be low across most of the CONUS on Friday,
   the exception being over the northern Gulf Coast late Friday night
   into Saturday morning.

   NHC currently forecasts Tropical Depression 9 to become a hurricane
   late Thursday, strengthening further into Friday over the Gulf of
   America. Some uncertainty exists as to the timing of an eventual
   forward acceleration northward. In any case, the system is forecast
   to affect the northern Gulf Coast late in the Day 3 period (which
   ends at 12Z Saturday morning), and as such, low probabilities for
   tornado risk have been added.

   Low-level shear/SRH will be very strong east of the storm center.
   The surface air mass may remain stable over the mainland until very
   close to 12Z Saturday, with a greater chance of larger SBCAPE over
   extreme southeast LA prior to 12Z. Once the coastal boundary moves
   inland, a surge of mid 70s F dewpoints and southerly winds will lead
   to overly enlarged hodographs, supporting rotation in the stronger
   cells with tornado potential.

   ..Jewell.. 10/07/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
